A channel is a graph place

A channel is not a chat list. It is a durable entity where people, teammates, messages, subchannels, threads, and shared work keep their own identities and relationships.

Solid ink — shipped graph semantics Ghost ink — the depicted channel interface is designed, not shipped verified against the live edge registry on 2026-08-20

01Build the place

Drive one sequence. A subchannel branches off, a reply becomes a thread, and a task enters the channel without losing its task identity. Switch to the identity map at any step to see what the stream is made of.

02Equal citizens, different fields

“Equal” means both can be named, addressed, related, and returned later. It does not mean a message and a task have the same schema.

Entity

01a09f21-4c00-7a11-8b2e-0d3f5a7c9e11

A task keeps its kind, version, status, and relationships when it is attached to a channel. Sharing does not flatten it into message text.

=

Message

01a09c30-3000-7000-8000-ddddddddddd4

A message is also an entity. It keeps an author and durable id, and the server projects its anchor as anchored_to.

ChannelAn entity with a durable id and version. has_member links members and teammates; it is a roster, not an ACL or subscription.
SubchannelAnother channel whose parentId points to a channel in the same Space. Hierarchy remains same-kind.
ThreadDurable messages on the channel anchor. A reply carries its parent message id; anchored_to is the server-derived graph projection.
Shared taskThe task stays a task. attached_to can target a channel and powers channel context shelves; a stream reference points back to the same task id.

03The address survives the moment

You can post to the channel because every entity is an anchor: tm8 message send --to <channel-id> "Investigating the redirect". Later, the channel, the task, and each message still have their own durable handles. The conversation is not froth around the graph; it is part of the graph.

Honest statusThe server-side channel kind, hierarchy, roster relationship, message anchoring, reply threading, and context attachment are shipped. The channel interface depicted above is next-phase work, so its frame is dashed. Voice channels are outside this lesson.
